content.comment_body: Hello all, Is it possible to configure [product_name] memory to be retentive? Specifically, if I turn on an M bit and then power off, will its state remain after power is restored? Please advise. Thank you. [user_name]

Are you using a Set-Reset latch to modify the memory bit state? Try the method of setting retentiveness in the latching relay function block properties. Refer to the provided image for guidance. Please let us know if this helps.

Hi [user_name], You can achieve this by using a special function block like a pulse relay after your M flag. In [product_name] programming software, double-click the pulse relay to open its properties, where you'll find a 'retentivity' checkbox. Enabling it will retain the block's state after power restoration. If you have further questions, feel free to ask. Best regards, [user_name]

When you enable retentivity in the block properties of, for example, a pulse relay, [product_name] will store the last state of that block, even if the power is turned off. You can simulate this in the [product_name] programming software using the plug icon in simulation mode to test power loss.
Hello [user_name], Standard memory bits are not retentive; you need to use a dedicated block, double-click it, and enable retentivity in its settings.
Hello, Thank you for your help, the answer was clear. How many latching relays can be used in a [product_name] RC [article_no]? Thanks, [user_name]

The number of latching relays available depends on the [product_name] version. The article number ends in [article_no], indicating the version. Check the attached image: the top shows hardware selection and available resources; the bottom displays what your program has used if hardware is selected. Keep in mind that enabling 'retentive' options consumes memory in addition to function blocks. Experiment with these options and resources in your program to become familiar. Enjoy exploring.

In [product_name] programming software: Press CTRL + H or go via Tools > Select Hardware. Choose your [product_name] model, and you'll see detailed information regarding blocks, memory usage, and more.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are asking how to make memory bits in [product_name] retentive so their state is preserved after a power cycle. Community members explain that standard memory bits are not retentive, but using specialized blocks like pulse relay or latching relay with retentivity enabled in the software will achieve this. There were questions about the maximum number of latching relays supported and how retentive settings affect available device memory. The intuitive simulation and hardware selection tools in the programming software are seen as beneficial and encourage experimentation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a straightforward way to configure [product_name] memory bits or function blocks for persistent status after power restoration, expecting reliable retention of critical data through power cycles.
